title: A Signal for the Machine
premise: Jonah Zhou, a clone grown from the memories of a murdered astronomer, tends a deep-space beacon whose true purpose was erased along with the original's killer. When gravity stutters for nine seconds across the whole system, Jonah's beacon is revealed as the only thing keeping two hostile fleets from open war—both sides believing the other fired first. To prevent genocide, Jonah must sustain a forged 'Earth transmission' proving the original was assassinated to fake that signal, while falling for Ilsa Reyes, the investigator sent to silence them. In the end Jonah broadcasts the original's final, hidden testimony, forcing both fleets to confront a common enemy—the corporation that built the clone—and chooses love and exile over the duty of staying invisible.
about_author: Petra Almeida is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction from a decommissioned listening station in the Azores. Her work explores inherited memory, bureaucratic violence, and the people who maintain machines no one remembers building.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. During a routine beacon calibration, gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds; every clock Jonah owns disagrees afterward. The emotional beat is quiet dread—the sense that the universe just blinked at them personally.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: Jonah reflects on waking as a clone of Dr. Elias Zhou, murdered before the clone's decanting, inheriting only his memories and his unmaintained beacon. Flashbacks establish the original's paranoia. Beat: grief for a life that was never quite yours.

chapters.title: Traffic That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The nine-second event left sensor ghosts—two fleet formations that briefly became visible to each other and to the beacon. Jonah realizes their station recorded the anomaly. Beat: the terror of being noticed after years of deliberate obscurity.

chapters.title: Ilsa Comes Up the Dock
chapters.summary: Ilsa Reyes, an investigator with corporate credentials and a private agenda, arrives claiming to audit the beacon. Jonah lies badly about the recordings. Beat: wary attraction sharpened by the knowledge that she may be the original's killer's colleague.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She reviews Jonah's logs, suspecting the clone is a corporate failsafe, and finds encrypted fragments of the original's final transmission loop. Beat: her growing suspicion that her employers sent her to bury a crime, not solve one.

chapters.title: The Lie Between Fleets
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah deciphers the original's notes: the beacon broadcasts a forged 'Earth transmission' that both fleets interpret as proof of neutral arbitration. If it stops, they war. Beat: the crushing weight of inheriting a lie as a duty.

chapters.title: Calibration at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: A fleet patrol docks, demanding beacon access. Ilsa covers for Jonah with a forged audit, burning her first professional bridge. Beat: the first choice of loyalty over duty—and the fear of what that costs.

chapters.title: Memories That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A memory fragment surfaces of the original meeting someone the night before his murder—a woman with a Reyes-family insignia. Jonah begins to suspect Ilsa's mother. Beat: love curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: The Loop Is Ending
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She discovers the forged transmission is a finite loop, degrading, with weeks left before both fleets hear static. Her employers know. Beat: the horror of realizing the peace was always a countdown.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Jonah and Ilsa admit what they each know over shared rations in the beacon's core. Neither fully trusts the other; both want to. Beat: intimacy as an act of courage.

chapters.title: The Second Flicker
chapters.summary: Gravity stutters again—longer, localized around the beacon. Someone is testing whether the anomaly can be weaponized to frame one fleet. Beat: the invisible enemy takes shape: the clone-foundry, Halcyon Biogenic.

chapters.title: Murder, Restaged
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She finds Halcyon's plan: reproduce the original's murder using the clone as the corpse, closing the case forever. Beat: cold fury—the corporation intends to erase Jonah the way it erased the truth.

chapters.title: Run the Long Dark
chapters.summary: Jonah and Ilsa flee the beacon in a maintenance skiff with the original's data cores, pursued by Halcyon security. Beat: fugitive adrenaline and the strange freedom of finally being seen.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the First Signal
chapters.summary: They shelter in the original's hidden lab inside a derelict relay, where the full murder testimony is stored—naming Halcyon's directors and the forged signal's architect. Beat: the original becomes a person, not a ghost.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The transmission loop degrades ahead of schedule; both fleets go to alert. Jonah must choose: keep the lie alive with a new forgery, or tell the truth and risk everything. Beat: duty and honesty at war.

chapters.title: What Ilsa Was Sent to Do
chapters.summary: Ilsa confesses: her original orders were to kill the clone and certify the case closed. She never intended to obey—but Jonah must decide whether to believe her. Beat: love against duty, stated plainly and painfully.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax begins. From the derelict relay, they splice the original's testimony into the dying transmission loop, broadcasting truth to both fleets simultaneously. Halcyon scrambles to jam them. Beat: defiant hope.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds to Decide
chapters.summary: Halcyon triggers a final gravity weapon to destroy the relay; the fleets, having heard the testimony, each hesitate for nine seconds—long enough for Jonah to redirect the blast into Halcyon's own staging fleet. Beat: the climax's cost.

chapters.title: After the Static
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Both fleets convene an ad hoc tribunal outside any lawful jurisdiction; Halcyon's directors are named and abandoned by their own shareholders. Beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfect and earned.

chapters.title: The Case of Elias Zhou
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The murder is formally closed—not with a verdict against a person, but against a system. Jonah mourns the original properly for the first time. Beat: grief finally given room.

chapters.title: A Beacon, Recommissioned
chapters.summary: The fleets jointly recommission the beacon as an honest arbitration relay, and offer Jonah the post. Ilsa resigns her commission. Beat: found family forming from former adversaries and a clone who was never supposed to matter.

chapters.title: The First True Transmission
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, coda. Jonah and Ilsa send the beacon's first authentic message—a simple acknowledgment, signed by both of them—and watch the acknowledgments come back from two fleets at once. Beat: quiet, earned peace; visibility chosen at last.
